description: Observed-order-of-accuracy sweep for grids/latlon3d/rules/varcoeff_laplacian_lev_noflux_bc (conservative finite-volume variable-coefficient vertical diffusion d/dz(kz du/dz) on the non-uniform vertical, zero-flux at the surface and the model top) driven by problems/latlon3d_diffusion_vertical_noflux.esm. Refines NLEV alone (16 -> 128) with lon and lat passive at NLON = 8, NLAT = 5, since the operator is purely vertical. Manufactured solution u(z,t) = exp(-pi^2 t) cos(pi z) on a quadratic-stretch mesh with a parabolic boundary-layer diffusivity kz = 0.5(1 + 4z(1-z)); the gradient vanishes at both walls, so the physical flux matches the zero-flux closure exactly. SECOND ORDER in both L2 and Linf (observed 2.00 / 2.00). The measured quantity is the SOLUTION error at t = 0.1, not the raw truncation error: this operator's interior truncation is O(dz^2) but its two boundary cells are O(dz), because imposing the EXACT wall flux breaks the leading-order cancellation between neighbouring face-flux errors that the interior enjoys. The parabolic solve smooths that boundary-localised defect back to O(dz^2) globally (Gustafsson), which is the physically meaningful order and the one gated here. The alternative -- a formally higher-order boundary closure -- would cost exact mass conservation, which for a tracer-transport operator is the wrong trade.
